item.title: Infracom Mail 0.6.0
item.description:
- Flag a message and it stays findable: a Flagged view in the sidebar lists
  everything you have starred, across every folder, and a flagged message that
  you then archive stays in the list and says where it went.
- The flag is the same state IMAP calls \Flagged, so a message starred in Apple
  Mail or Outlook shows as flagged here, and one flagged here shows as flagged
  there.
- A message you have already replied to is marked in the list, so you no longer
  have to open a thread to find out whether you answered it.
- The sidebar shows how full the mailbox is, amber near the limit and red when
  full. Deployments that set no limit show no gauge.
- A file too large to attach is refused when you pick it, naming its size and
  the limit, instead of failing at the end of the upload.
- A draft written in another mail client and addressed to somebody outside the
  company shows the address it was written to, rather than appearing to be
  addressed to nobody.

item.title: Infracom Mail 0.5.0
item.description:
- Save Draft keeps the message and the window: it used to spin the Send button,
  which read as the half-written message going out, and then close.
- Reply, Reply All, Forward, Mark as Read/Unread, Archive, Move to Trash and Get
  New Mail are in a Message menu with the shortcuts every other Mac mail client
  uses, and the Delete key acts on the selected messages.
- Replies and forwards are written in the compose font instead of AppKit's Times
  12, and the quoted message is set in from the reply rather than running into
  it.
- The composer checks spelling as you type.
- A compose window is named after the message in it, not "New Message".
- The caret starts in the body of a reply or a resumed draft, and in To on a
  blank message.
- A send retried after a failure replays the first attempt rather than
  delivering the message twice.
- The autocomplete list stays with the row it was typed in, so results from To
  cannot be picked from under Cc.
- A link typed as "example.com" is understood, and one that cannot be read says
  so instead of greying the Add button out.
- One destructive toolbar button, named for what it does in the folder you are
  in ("Move to Trash", "Discard Draft", "Delete Permanently"), and every
  message-action button has a tooltip.
- List dates from another year say which year.
- Clicking a new-mail banner opens that message, and a banner appears even while
  the app is frontmost.
- Removing a saved account from the login window asks first, and its button sits
  beside the card rather than inside it.
- Contacts shows that it is loading instead of claiming an empty directory.
- The splash clears once the session has settled, and Escape skips it.
- The message list takes a multiple selection again: shift-click, cmd-click and
  Select All Messages (Cmd-Shift-A), with Mark Read, Archive, Trash and Delete
  acting on all of them at once.
- Refresh says whether it is working, and a refresh that fails over a folder
  that already has messages in it puts a banner above the list instead of
  leaving a stale list looking current.
- Opening a thread marks every unread message in it read, not only the one
  clicked, and the thread scrolls to that message and outlines it.
- A reply landing in the thread you are reading now appears there, rather than
  only in the list and the badges.
- Drafts is badged with how many drafts there are.
- Searching keeps paging: typing a query used to stop the list loading any more
  messages, so nothing further could ever enter the search. Switching folder
  clears the query rather than opening the next folder pre-filtered by it.
- Message rows tell VoiceOver whether they are unread and whether they have
  attachments.
- Attachments are fetched once and reused, instead of being downloaded again
  every time a card is drawn; saving one asks where to put it before it starts,
  so cancelling no longer throws away a finished download.
- An inline image whose bytes could not be fetched is offered as a download
  instead of leaving a placeholder nothing can reach.
- Colours a sender chose are kept where they can be read and lifted where they
  cannot: a dark grey body colour is no longer a smudge on the dark card, a
  yellow highlight stays black on yellow instead of white on yellow, and mail
  carrying this client's old baked-in dark colours no longer draws as charcoal
  bars in light mode.
- Reopening a draft keeps the pictures in it embedded, rather than shipping a
  dead file:/// reference and the picture as a loose attachment.
- Removing an embedded image's chip removes the picture too, so the message
  cannot go out pointing at a part that is no longer attached.
- The plain-text part of a message with a picture in it no longer carries a
  stray object-replacement character into list snippets and IMAP clients.
- A contact with no office reads "Not set" rather than a stray comma.

item.title: Infracom Mail 0.4.0
item.description:
- An unfinished message can no longer be destroyed. It is written to Drafts a
  couple of seconds after you stop typing, when you close the compose window,
  and when a reply or a new message takes the window over, which used to throw
  the half-written one away with no warning.
- A name typed into To, Cc or Bcc counts. Return turns it into a recipient, the
  arrow keys walk the suggestions, and a message will not go out leaving a name
  behind in the field.
- Attaching a file shows a chip and a spinner straight away, and Send waits for
  the upload instead of sending the message without it.
- Drafts can be discarded, from the row's own menu or the toolbar.
- Right-clicking a message no longer opens it in the reading pane or marks it
  read on its way to being archived, and Delete inside Trash asks first, as the
  toolbar's Delete already did.
- Actions that fail say so. Archiving, deleting, resuming a draft and the folder
  counts all reported failures nowhere at all.
- Checking for new mail every 30 seconds no longer throws away the pages you
  have scrolled through.
- Searching says it only searched what has been downloaded, and offers to fetch
  more, instead of announcing "No Results" for mail that exists.
- Cmd-Z after a formatting button takes back the formatting. It used to replay
  the typing record and delete the text you had written.
- Replies and forwards keep the pictures from the message being answered, and a
  picture you insert is the one your Content-ID points at.
- Screenshots wider than the reading pane are scaled to fit instead of being
  drawn at full size with the right-hand side clipped off.

item.title: Infracom Mail 0.3.4
item.description:
- Message bodies are visible again. Since 0.3.0 every body was laid out with
  no height at all, so messages appeared empty.
- Mail you send no longer carries your appearance's colours. Writing in dark
  mode was hard-coding light grey text into the message, which read badly for
  anyone in light mode.
- Mail that arrives with light text and no background to sit on is recoloured
  so it stays readable.

item.title: Infracom Mail 0.3.3
item.description:
- Attached images show a thumbnail instead of only their filename, so you can
  see what was sent without saving it first.
- Updates install. The released builds carried a malformed entitlement, so the
  updater was refused permission to talk to its own installer.

item.title: Infracom Mail 0.3.2
item.description:
- An image placed in a message you send now arrives inside it. It was being
  dropped from the message on the way out, so it turned up as a plain
  attachment instead, and looked wrong in your own Sent folder.

item.title: Infracom Mail 0.3.1
item.description:
- Updates install. Finding one worked; applying it failed with "An error
  occurred while launching the installer" because the app was missing the key
  that tells Sparkle a sandboxed app installs through its XPC service.

item.title: Infracom Mail 0.3.0
item.description:
- Embedded images show in the message instead of appearing as files to
  download, including pictures in mail written in Outlook.
- Compose can place an image inside the message, at the caret.
- A picture the message embeds is no longer also listed as an attachment.

item.title: Infracom Mail 0.2.2
item.description:
- Automatic updates work. 0.2.1 shipped a fix that was the wrong one: Sparkle
  keeps its helper services inside its own framework, and moving them into the
  app was itself a fatal updater error, so no update check ever ran.

item.title: Infracom Mail 0.2.1
item.description:
- Messages and replies follow the system appearance. Mail written in Outlook
  carries an explicit black on its text, which stayed black in dark mode and
  left whole messages unreadable.
- Replying while a compose window is already open now fills in the recipient
  and subject, instead of reusing the open window's blank state.
- Fixed automatic updates failing to start on this sandboxed app.
- Setting a PIN explains what it changes before you choose one, shows a caret
  so it is clear the boxes are taking typing, can reveal what you typed, and
  can be changed in one step rather than removed and set again.

item.title: Infracom Mail 0.2.0
item.description:
- Sign in on a Mac with a six-character PIN instead of a username and password.
  The saved session is encrypted with the PIN, so it is the only way back in on
  that machine; five wrong attempts removes it and asks for the password.
- The login window now puts the caret in the field it is asking for: the
  password when the account is already known, the username otherwise.
- Automatic updates.
